sections.content: How many people are "nursing auxiliaries and assistants"?

294,450 people

were counted on the census as "nursing auxiliaries and assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Nursing auxiliaries and assistants help doctors, nurses and other health professionals in caring for the sick and injured within hospitals, homes, clinics and the wider community.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "nursing auxiliaries and assistants" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "nursing auxiliaries and assistants", 12% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "nursing auxiliaries and assistants" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "nursing auxiliaries and assistants" included:

  • science, engineering and production technicians (other)
  • elementary process plant occupations (other)
  • care workers and home carers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "nursing auxiliaries and assistants" there were more women than men (79.3% compared with 20.7%).

This means "nursing auxiliaries and assistants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 20.7% and women made up 79.3% of "nursing auxiliaries and assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "nursing auxiliaries and assistants" included:

  • psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists
  • librarians
  • counsellors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "nursing auxiliaries and assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "nursing auxiliaries and assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "nursing auxiliaries and assistants", 12.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (60.3% compared with 39.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.9%) than self-employed (2.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
